claims.text: The pattern-matching baseline model achieved a 77.33% average overall accuracy across nine SDoH aspects.
openchat_3.5 achieved over 40% higher average Accuracy_mentioned than the pattern-matching baseline model.
Llama-2-13b-chat was the only evaluated LLM with a significantly lower average Accuracy_mentioned compared to the baseline.
Two human reviewers achieved 93% inter-annotator agreement on manual labeling of 9 SDoH aspects across 200 patient records.
The pattern-matching baseline model achieved an average Accuracy_non-mentioned of 96.66%.
Model quantization did not substantially compromise LLM performance on SDoH extraction tasks.

evidence.description: The baseline model achieved a 77.33% average Accuracyoverall, which was mainly attributable to its high average Accuracynon-mentioned.
Openchat_3.5 achieved over 40% higher of the average Accuracy mentioned than the baseline, which shows its superior capability in extracting information when it is contained in free text.
On the other hand, Llama-2-13b-chat was the only LLM that had a significantly worse average Accuracymentioned compared to the baseline.

The inter-annotator agreement was calculated based on the total number of the 1800 questions (9 SdoH questions * 200 patients) that the two annotators agreed before discussion among all the 1800 questions, which was 93%.
We found that the baseline achieved an average Accuracy non-mentioned of 96.66%.
We also observed that quantization, which could make these models more applicable in resource limited settings, did not substantially compromise the performance on extraction tasks.

methodologies.name: Zero-shot open-source LLM extraction pipeline with prompt engineering
methodologies.description: A question-answering framework using eight open-source LLMs with prompt engineering, AWQ quantization, and post-processing pattern matching to extract nine SDoH categories from unstructured clinical notes.
conditions: Zero-shot prompting with default vs. refined prompt engineering
Evaluated on 100 validation and 100 test patient clinical notes against manual annotations

limitations.text: Traditional rule-based NLP approaches are constrained by their lack of generalizability across different datasets and settings.
Machine learning-based NLP models rely heavily on the costly step of manual data annotation for model training, making them harder to scale.
The prompt engineering and LLM response postprocessing steps involve complexity and subjectivity.
Observations regarding model performance based on general SDoH concepts may not extrapolate to other, more complex clinical feature extraction tasks.
Premise prompts designed to reduce hallucination in the refined pipeline reduced sensitivity to SDoH features mentioned in the text.

future_work.text: Conduct specific training or fine-tuning of open-source LLMs on free-text EHRs for extracting more complex clinical concepts.
